In order to discharge this responsibility, and to keep the existing streets and highways from deteriorating, these agencies are constantly making improvements as to surface conditions, safety and efficiency of operation.
As early as December 1963 the City of Milwaukee's street improvement program called for the reconstruction of Grange Avenue from Howell Avenue to the North-South Freeway (I-94). Existing Grange Avenue was scheduled to be completely replaced with an ultimate highway section consisting of two 42-foot roadways separated by a 22-foot median. Right of way requirements of Grange Avenue would have been 110 feet with no control of access. Since that time, Milwaukee County has also been striving to obtain FHWA approval for access to the Interstate System to service the airport at General Mitchell Field. In response to increased congestion on airport access routes Milwaukee County by Federal directive, initiated a proposal linking General Mitchell Field to the nearest Interstate Route. This proposal requested an access interchange at I-94 with ramp facilities to the local arterial street system at Grange Avenue.
Although these proposals were rejected by FHWA, access was granted to I-94 (North-South Freeway) in September 1967.
